title: sparse-context-anchor-format-sketch
content:
Purpose:

This is a personal sketch for a compact, forward-compatible on-disk / on-wire format for sparse context anchors. Idea: lightweight index that lets caller/edge/client request only the small set of context snippets (anchors) likely to be useful for a given prompt. Designed to be efficient for storage in KV (Dynamo/Redis/Bigtable-like) and fast to transfer as a delta over network for session resumption or client-side prefetch.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Extremely compact per-anchor representation (aim ~80-300 bytes typical)
- Versioned and extensible so runtime can add metadata without breaking older clients
- Support anchor relevance weights, TTL, provenance, and small routing hints
- Allow delta updates (append-only or chunk diff) for cheap session sync
- Work cross-environment: hosted, dedicated, private (no external deps)

Intuition / semantics:
- "Anchor" = short context snippet + small semantic fingerprint + weight + meta. Not a full blob. Anchors are pointers for prefetch/recall; application may fetch full block separately.
- Anchors are generated by runtime or client based on prompt/interaction. They are not truth: must be validated when used (quality guardrails).

File/Record layout (ASCII sketch):

| HEADER (fixed) | ANCHOR_TABLE (var) | FOOTER (opt checksums) |

HEADER (32 bytes target):
- magic: 4B = "SPAR"
- version: 1B (uint8)
- flags: 1B (bitflags - e.g., compressed, delta, encrypted)
- anchor_count: 2B (uint16)
- anchor_index_offset: 4B (uint32, bytes from start)
- timestamp_ms: 8B (uint64)
- reserved: 12B (padding -> future)

Anchor entry (variable, compact):
- id_len: 1B (0-255)
- id: id_len bytes (opaque id: base62 or trimmed uuid)
- fp_len: 1B
- fingerprint: fp_len bytes (e.g., 8-16 bytes; simhash or blake2 short digest)
- weight: 1B (0-255 mapped to 0.0-1.0)
- ttl_secs: 4B (uint32)
- src_tag_len: 1B
- src_tag: src_tag_len bytes (e.g., "user:msg" | "kb:faq-23")
- flags: 1B (bitflags: pinned, redacted, ephemeral)
- offset_or_ref: 4B (uint32) -> optional pointer to full blob in a companion store or sequence number
- compact_text_len: 2B (uint16)
- compact_text: compact_text_len bytes (UTF-8)  -- usually 32-256 bytes trimmed/summarized

Notes on fields:
- id: per-anchor short opaque id. If client stores anchors locally, id enables dedupe and de-duplication across sessions.
- fingerprint: for fast LSH-like lookup on server-side and cheap equality checks.
- weight: single byte allows cheap ranking; runtime maps to actual score.
- ttl_secs: 0 == no-expiry; helpers in runtime to expire stale anchors.
- offset_or_ref: 0 means no external reference. If non-zero, it's an index into a companion append-log or block store used to fetch full context chunk.
- compact_text: best-effort summary or context slice. Must be human-readable for debugging.

On-wire API shapes (REST-ish examples)
- GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/anchors?since=seq&limit=64 -> returns AnchorBundle (binary or JSON)
- POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/anchors -> accept new anchors (batch) as compressed bundle; server replies with acks and assigned anchor ids

Binary vs JSON envelope:
- Production: use binary packed (above) for performance. Fallback: json with same fields for debugging.

AnchorBundle JSON example (for debug):
{
  "version": "1",
  "session": "s-3456",
  "anchors": [
    {"id":"a1","fp":"3f9b...","w":200,"ttl":3600,"src":"user:reply","ref":1234,"text":"Bought milk on 2025-11-08"}
  ],
  "timestamp":"2025-11-08T14:35:02Z"
}

Delta update model:
- Each session has a monotonic seq number. Anchors posted with seq N. Clients can request all anchors since seq K. Server can return "deleted" tombstones with id + tombstone flag.
- To reduce network: we include bloom/sketch of ids in header (optional flag) so client can quickly detect whether it already has anchors. Bloom serialized in footer.

Indexing and lookup strategies (runtime notes):
- Primary store: Append log + compact index. Append entry stores full blob; index stores the compact anchor record above.
- Secondary store: per-tenant (or per-tenant-shard) Redis/rocksdb mapping from anchor-fingerprint -> anchor-id list for fast retrieval during reranking
- Retrieval flow when serving a prompt: compute fingerprint of prompt, probe LSH; get candidate anchor ids; fetch compact anchors; rank by weight + match score; if candidate needs full blob, fetch via offset/ref from block store.

Compaction and GC:
- Background compaction job groups anchors by fingerprint similarity and drops duplicates (keep highest weight or newest).
- TTL and tombstones: tombstones are kept for T_grace (e.g., 24h) to prevent resurrecting anchors from older clients.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Anchors may include sensitive phrases (compact_text). Default: compact_text is redacted or hashed unless explicitly allowed by user/tenant config. Use flags bit to mark redaction.
- If encrypted flag set in header, body is encrypted with tenant key (KMS). Avoid leaking fingerprints if privacy policy requires. Consider salted fingerprints for per-tenant isolation.

Compatibility / versioning: 
- version byte in header -> any unknown fields are skipped using anchor_index_offset.
- Optional per-anchor TLV area for future fields (JSON chunk per-anchor) but this bloats size; prefer small TLV types for common items.

Example compact-anchor (human readable)
- id: "u7Xk"
- fp: 8 bytes (b"\x9a\x88...")
- w: 210 (0.82)
- ttl: 86400
- src: "kb:pricing-4"
- flags: pinned
- ref: 40233
- text: "Pricing table row, discount tiers, 2025-11 revision"

ASCII diagram for client prefetch sequence:

Client                      Edge Cache                     Server
   |------prewarm request (since=100)-------------------->|
   |<-----AnchorBundle (binary, 12 anchors + bloom)-------|
   (locally merge anchors, dedupe by id/fp)
   | if prompt needs anchors -> lookup local anchors -> select top 3
   | if anchor ref missing -> fetch full block from Edge/Server

Open questions / TODOs (brain dump):
- Should fingerprint be salted per-tenant to prevent cross-tenant correlation? Tradeoff: salted fp breaks cross-tenant dedupe and sharing. Probably per-tenant salt as default, opt-out for global index.
- What is acceptable compact_text budget? 64 bytes seems small; 256 bytes increases transfer costs. Maybe variable based on weight/importance.
- How do we handle large numbers of anchors per session? cap at N=1024? evict by weight-age policy.
- Offline-cold resumption: if client has a cached anchor bundle aged >30d, server needs TTL checks and possibly revalidate anchors.
- Concurrency model: who owns id generation? Client or server? If client generates short id, collision risk; server-assigned ids need ack latency.
- Do we need canonical canonicalization for compact_text to improve dedupe? (strip emails, numbers)

Bench plan (microbench to run):
- Serialized binary size / anchor for average: measure across 1k real anchors sample set
- Latency: save -> fetch -> apply flow in edge cache under 95th percentile load
- Cost: bytes transferred for typical session resume (local 3 anchors vs naive full context 3KB)

Notes to self: keep this intentionally small and iterative. Start with v1 minimal header + anchor table + footer checksum. Avoid embedding full JSON per anchor initially.

References / inspiration:
- local-llm-session-proposal (internal note)
- memcached style append-log and cold object store patterns
- LSH fingerprint work in applied-ml team (Lina)

Next steps:
- Convert to a runnable spec: implement python serializer/deserializer, test with existing session store samples (Diego to share sample dumps), run size/latency bench.
- Draft a short RFC and flag privacy implications for privacy/security review.

-- A.K.
